title: I'm stuck on pathing
author: kalvinbastello
selftext:
On this for for a solid two weeks and not sure what to do now. I've spent a few months developing a game and all I have left to do is balance the combat. For sake of argument lets call it a tower defense that has scattered random generated paths and a builder. 

I can get the builder to have good collision with the pathing that it weaves in and out of and even makes holes in walls, but for the life of me I can't get AI to path to the builder without jumping through non existent holes in the wall, teleporting to builder, or just going directly to builder and getting stuck on a wall inbetween. 



I've used GPT 5.1 Mini for the first half and 5.3 codex when it became available for the second half of game. Whenever I got stuck Copilot was actually able to figure out the issues quickly, but not this time. I even tried using Claude Opus 4.7 to debug and fix to no avail.

  
Where do I go from here?

comments.author: c0desurfer
comments.body: Maybe recast & detour would help here? I used it back then for World of Wacraft bots. It seems there is even a JS lib out there, see [https://github.com/isaac-mason/recast-navigation-js](https://github.com/isaac-mason/recast-navigation-js) (throw it at your AI agent).

replies.author: kalvinbastello
replies.body: So AI says this wouldn't work because fundamentally a 3D tool used for geometry navigation, not really 2D and certainly not tiles. It would have to convert to geometry then voxalize it Everytime something changes.

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
you should just do some research to get some conceptual understanding of pathing

for example, pathing is relatively straight forward if you have a 2d top-down grid. A common approach like A\* would work just fine. Some game engine already have A\* pathing built-in too

I think it gets trickier once you have elevations and a gridless terrain etc so you have to look into what other people do commonly

replies.author: MinimusMaximizer
replies.body: Even naive breadth first search should work and using either buzzword will inform the AI what to try.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body: yes, BFS is another staple. there are also some "dumb" ways to do pathing like a sensory approach e.g. roomba

replies.author: kalvinbastello
replies.body: I think this is what I need to do if I don't have a grid? But so far the attempts at pathing as I'm reading the output, isn't working. Still getting stuck trying to find its way.

replies.author: R3v153
replies.body:
Sounds like you could easily throw this into a tile based array and place a value for each tile. Run a A\* algorithm using the weight values of each tile.. if there is a wall it is set to something like 999 etc.. or even 0 to define non walkable areas.. paths sets to 1.. all others you can define a range and it will pick a path based on the values. 

You do not need to organize your layout into grids for your aesthetics.. you can just get the math to create the grid based on position values of your objects.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
if the aesthetics doesn't match the grid, it may look off. 

but yes, basically what you said. 

I think OP is struggling probably because he/she is doing something non grid based and he/she is trying to improvise a pathing solution

replies.author: R3v153
replies.body:
True. Thanks, I should have clarified that the granularity is the resolution of the tile map. The higher the resolution (meaning less pixels per tile) the tighter the control but more CPU to find the pathing. 

Now that I reread the post it sounds like a navmesh generated at runtime may be the best way if not using a tile map. I have seen a few tools around that could help

replies.author: kalvinbastello
replies.body: Ah. I don't have a grid. I have walls that are offset and randomly generated so some natural gaps others aren't passable without punching holes on them.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
there are some non-grid pathing strategies so look into them and see what you have to adjust with the map

you mention tower defense so you may need an efficient solution too so your game doesn't lag with a large number of enemies

I use Unity and Unity has navmesh obstacles so "the real time placement of obstacles affecting pathing" is basically a built-in feature of the game engine

replies.author: kalvinbastello
replies.body: It talks about this being a flow field solution the just needs adjustment, but I'm pretty out of my depth of how to guide it better

replies.author: R3v153
replies.body:
Here is an article.. would suggest reading it, or I guess just get AI to read it for you. 

https://www.redblobgames.com/blog/2024-04-27-flow-field-pathfinding/

Basically you define a vector field of the entire map. Each vector points in the direction of movement for location. This solution is used in games with high number of agents as the pathing can be localized to just the area of the agent.  You don’t have to have tiles to do this..  you just need to find that sweet spot between a small enough pixel count per vector and not too many vectors to crash a CPU. Define your map size (1000x1000) and size for the vector cells.. 10 pixels per vector.. that’s a 100x100 grid ( 10,000 vectors). 

No clue if this is an option for you though.

comments.author: Puzzleheaded-Way542
comments.body:
You want a heat map/vector field precalc'd over your map. This provides a direction and value to the nearest wall/collision point for any location and can be stored as a low resolution image even. 

Then enemy ai references this when moving towards a target and builds a path quickly.

Add in some randomization and path smoothing/bezier to the determine path targets and you got a pretty flawless collision avoiding pathing fast calc.
